title: The denominator changes as well
question: Why do two ordinary-looking speeds not simply add?
recap: Velocity is a ratio of a spatial difference to a time difference. Transform both differences before dividing, and light speed stays c while collinear subluminal speeds compose below c.
premises: Use the same two neighboring events on a particle’s trajectory.
Frames are inertial and the boost is along x.
limitations: The plus-sign composition formula and a passive frame change have different stated directions.
Non-collinear boosts generally include a rotation, not only another aligned boost.

overview.text: Velocity is a ratio of a spatial difference to a time difference. Transform both differences before dividing, and light speed stays c while collinear subluminal speeds compose below c.

full.spoken: The transformed longitudinal velocity is u x minus v over one minus v u x over c squared; transverse velocity has the same denominator and an additional gamma.

full.text: To describe an object moving at w along the moving frame’s positive axis in the original frame, use the inverse relation U = (v + w)/(1 + vw/c²). With v = w = 0.6c, U is 15c/17, about 0.88235c, not 1.2c.

For a right-moving light ray u_x = c, the passive transformation also gives c. The velocity-composition laboratory shows the difference from Galilean addition without clamping a superluminal arithmetic result.

full.returnCaption: Return to why do two ordinary-looking speeds not simply add.

items: Differentiate x′ = γ(x − vt) along the trajectory.
Differentiate t′ = γ(t − vx/c²) along that same trajectory.
Divide dx′ by dt′ only after both have been transformed.
For transverse motion use dy′ = dy but retain the transformed time denominator.
Use the inverse relation for the plus-sign composition of two forward speeds.
Distinguish aligned composition from the general non-collinear case.

margin.text: Rapidity and matrix composition are optional modern aids. They must not be treated as additional 1904 premises, nor should the group property erase the rotation associated with non-collinear boosts.
